claims.text: Hot rolling followed by rapid annealing will produce an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The inverted microstructure consists of discrete B2 precipitates dispersed within a continuous BCC matrix.
The B2 precipitates in the proposed microstructure will be coherent, nanoscale, and uniformly dispersed.
Typical two-phase B2+BCC refractory HEAs have a continuous ordered B2 matrix, high yield strength, and poor room-temperature ductility.
The poor ductility of typical B2+BCC refractory HEAs is attributable to the ordered B2 phase forming the continuous matrix.
An inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves ductility while maintaining high yield strength relative to the conventional continuous-B2 architecture.
The proposed processing will enhance yield strength, rather than merely maintain it.
The proposed strength and ductility benefit will persist during operation at 600–800°C under ion irradiation or helium implantation.
The inverted nanostructure will maintain the alloy's high-temperature and irradiation stability.
Rapid thermomechanical processing refines the grain structure and controls B2 precipitate size and distribution.
The dispersed B2 precipitates strengthen the alloy through dispersion strengthening.
A continuous BCC matrix facilitates dislocation motion and thereby improves ductility.
Maintaining a nanostructured architecture suppresses irradiation-induced defect growth.
Maintaining a nanostructured architecture suppresses irradiation-induced phase destabilization.
The beneficial response may be lost following substantial processing deviations or exposure to more extreme environmental conditions.
The optimal B2 precipitate size, volume fraction, and coherence for balancing strength and ductility under irradiation have not been quantified.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says yield strength will improve, while the predicted outcome permits yield strength to be merely maintained. The falsification rule nevertheless requires a statistically significant improvement in both yield strength and ductility, so a result with improved ductility and unchanged high yield strength would simultaneously satisfy the predicted outcome and trigger falsification.
